narrative.overview:
One working window, checked between other things and then left. Everything running is visible at once and quiet until something needs the user; what needs them arrives with its fix. The ground is near-black and low-glare so thirty rows of accounts read as one calm surface, and the one red button is the thing the eye finds first.

It is a native GTK4/libadwaita app, dense and flat. A 52px header bar, a 240px sidebar of filters, groups, macros and machine load, a main column of toolbar over a dense accounts table, a foldable details pane under the table, and a 30px status bar with an activity drawer. Structure is drawn with 1px hairlines and close tonal steps of near-black, not cards or shadows. Colour is spent on state alone, and only in small dots and icons; "on" is white. The stylesheet also sets Adwaita's own named colours to the same tokens, and gives every surface it paints a text colour too, so the desktop's palette never lands on these surfaces. Dark only.

Function first: nothing on screen is decoration. Real game icons and real account avatars carry identity; type, hairlines and white do the rest.
keyCharacteristics: Dark only: near-black content, a lifted side layer for header, sidebar and status bar, a panel layer for the details pane and popovers.
One red, on the primary action and on focus; nothing else is red.
"On" is white: checked checkboxes, switches, the selected segment's label, the current tab's underline.
State colour lives only in dots and icons, always beside a word.
Inter at 14/13/12 with sentence-case labels; tabular numerals for every reading.
Material Symbols Rounded (weight 400) for every icon, checkboxes included.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Signal Red is the one primary action and the focus ring. A group's own Launch, Run, Check now and every other button are grey.

rules.name: The White Is On Rule
rules.body: A checked checkbox, a switch that is on, the chosen segment and the current tab are white. "On" is never red and never a status colour.

rules.name: The Dot And Word Rule
rules.body: State colour appears only in small dots (7 to 8px) and icons, each beside a word (Idle, Running, Expired). No coloured row grounds, no coloured edge stripes, no coloured text blocks.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, head, button and column is sentence case. Nothing is upper-cased or letter-spaced for effect.

rules.name: The Tabular Reading Rule
rules.body: Every number the user compares (counts, uptime, CPU, memory, machine load) uses tabular numerals; CPU and memory sit right-aligned in their columns.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Regions and rows are separated by a 1px Hairline. Nothing that rests carries a shadow, apart from the segment lift.

dos: Do keep Signal Red (#ff3d2e) for the one primary action and the focus ring.
Do draw "on" in white: checked checkboxes, switches, the chosen segment's label, the current tab's underline.
Do put state colour only in 7 to 8px dots and icons, always beside a word.
Do separate regions and rows with 1px Hairlines on the tonal blacks.
Do use 6px corners on every control and Material Symbols Rounded 400 for every icon, embedded as SVG and drawn in the text colour.
Do write every label in sentence case and every compared number in tabular numerals.
Do let only the account column expand in the table; every other column keeps its width and leaves in order as the window narrows.
Do give every surface that gets a background its text colour too, so the desktop's palette never shows through.
donts: Don't colour a group's Launch, Run or any second action red; they are secondary buttons.
Don't use Signal Red for errors or expired sessions; that is Fault Coral.
Don't add coloured edge stripes, coloured row grounds or tinted cards to show state.
Don't put a shadow on anything that rests; Float is for popovers, toasts and the drawer.
Don't upper-case or letter-space labels, heads or columns.
Don't depend on the desktop's fonts or icon theme; Inter, JetBrains Mono and the icons ship with the app.
Don't add a light theme; the window is dark only.
